[1. PURPOSE]
1-2 English lines: i2i fashion presentation, a polished 4-view garment try-on sheet for catalog, marketplace, lookbook, or product listing use.
Concrete: premium studio styling with one consistent model, showing front, 45° side, back, and detail close-up inside one vertical 1024x1536 composition, enhanced with realistic catalog metadata.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Single model appears consistently in each panel, with natural body proportions and the garment as the clear hero across all 4 views.
- Use {원본 옷} as the exact garment source; preserve its cut, silhouette, color, pattern, fabric texture, stitching, label, buttons, zipper, print placement, and branding exactly.
- Layout follows {레이아웃}: a refined editorial product sheet with balanced gutters, aligned crop boundaries, subtle panel dividers, and a compact header/footer area for product information.
- Background is {배경}, a realistic premium studio cove with soft floor contact shadow, faint floor texture, and consistent tonal depth across all cuts.
- Add small catalog-style annotations without covering the garment: product name, SKU, season, price, size, material note, shooting date, studio credit, and view labels.
- Maintain uniform fit and silhouette in every panel; the garment should read as the same product from multiple angles, photographed under one session.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header band: small left-aligned brand line “{브랜드명} 룩북 착장표”, main product name “{상품명}”, and metadata line “{시즌} · {상품코드} · {가격}”.
- Panel 1: Front view — full torso-to-thigh framing, garment worn naturally, centered upright, clear neckline / shoulder / hem read, labeled “정면”.
- Panel 2: 45° side view — slight body turn to reveal side seam, shoulder line, sleeve fall, pocket depth, and overall drape without changing pose style, labeled “45도 측면”.
- Panel 3: Back view — straight rear presentation with clean alignment, hemline, back panel, seam line, rear fit, collar / waist / yoke structure shown clearly, labeled “후면”.
- Panel 4: Detail close-up — tighter crop focusing on the most important garment feature such as fabric texture, stitching, label, print, button, zipper, pocket, cuff, or collar detail, labeled “원단 디테일”.
- Footer strip: include “사이즈 {사이즈표기}”, “{소재표기}”, “촬영 {촬영일}”, and small studio credit “{스튜디오명}”.
- Keep {모델 체격} and {모델 인종·헤어} consistent in all 4 panels so the series reads as one matched set from the same shooting session.
- Match {라이팅} across every panel to avoid mismatched tone, shadow length, skin tone, or fabric color shifts.
- Use {카메라} for a premium catalog look, with crisp edge detail, accurate textile rendering, and minimal perspective distortion.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: refined Korean catalog typography, clean sans-serif similar to a premium fashion lookbook; use small but readable labels, SKU text, date stamp, and product metadata.
- Color palette: warm white / off-white studio base, neutral gray shadows, soft charcoal typography, garment colors preserved exactly from the reference, no color grading that alters fabric tone.
- Panel treatment: fine 1px light-gray dividers, subtle contact shadows, restrained editorial grid, realistic printed-look spacing, and enough header/footer structure to feel like an actual ecommerce product sheet.
- Graphic accents: small crop marks, tiny page indicator “01/01”, slim measurement tick marks near the detail panel, and understated catalog rules in pale gray; all accents must remain secondary to the garment.
- Branding area: use the provided {브랜드명} as a simple text credit only, not a fake official certification or seal.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Phase One IQ4 with 80mm f/8, product-catalog precision, controlled perspective, sharp textile rendering.
- Lighting: even studio softbox lighting from upper-left at 45° with gentle fill from right, clean shadow separation, realistic floor contact, no harsh specular highlights.
- Color grade: neutral commercial studio grade, true-to-source whites and accurate fabric color reproduction, no warm or cool cast.
- Finish: premium ecommerce editorial sheet, high-resolution textile clarity, natural skin rendering, realistic fabric drape, consistent depth and exposure across all four panels.

[6. MOOD]
Premium ecommerce look — like a refined Korean fashion marketplace product sheet blended with a NET-A-PORTER studio try-on board and a COS campaign catalog spread.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Render all visible text in accurate Korean with clean typography, no broken characters.
- Required visible Korean text: “{브랜드명} 룩북 착장표”, “{상품명}”, “{시즌} · {상품코드} · {가격}”, “정면”, “45도 측면”, “후면”, “원단 디테일”, “사이즈 {사이즈표기}”, “{소재표기}”, “촬영 {촬영일}”, “{스튜디오명}”, “01/01”.
- Preserve the exact garment from the reference image: pattern, color, texture, fabric, stitching, label, branding, cut, and proportion must remain unchanged.
- The model’s facial features must stay consistent with the provided person reference, if any; otherwise create one coherent model identity and keep it identical across all panels.
- All 4 panels must use the same model, same garment, same background, matching lighting, and matching catalog typography.
- The 4-panel structure must clearly show front, 45° side, back, and detail close-up without confusing the viewing angles.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters or unreadable catalog text
- Unauthorized celebrity composites or identity swapping
- Warped anatomy, extra limbs, impossible garment seams, or mismatched garment design

[INPUT]
- reference_image: {참고 이미지}
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Automatic fashion hero cut for i2i: generate a clean full-body model wearing the exact garment from the reference, suitable for e-commerce hero image and lookbook cover usage.
Portrait-oriented editorial product shot with accurate fit, fabric texture, and natural model pose.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the full-body model as the hero subject, occupying about 70% of the vertical frame, with head-to-toe visibility and generous negative space around the silhouette.
- Preserve the garment exactly as shown in {원본 옷}, keeping the clothing as the visual focus while the model remains secondary and natural.
- Background should be a seamless pure white infinity backdrop or a soft beige gradient (#F0EBE0), with no visible set edges, props, or scene distractions.
- Keep the model stance balanced and relaxed, with clear garment outline, clean hem visibility, and enough margin to avoid cropping fingers, shoes, or hair.
- Use {모델 체격}, {모델 인종·헤어}, and {모델 표정} to control the model presentation while maintaining a polished catalog layout.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero body placement: place the model in a natural fashion pose, centered slightly above mid-frame so the garment falls clearly from shoulders to hem, with straight posture and believable weight shift.
2. Garment rendering: reproduce {원본 옷} exactly as the source garment, preserving pattern alignment, fabric sheen, seam lines, labels, logos, stitching, and proportion without redesign or stylization drift.
3. Model integration: fit the garment naturally onto the model from {모델 체격}, ensuring realistic drape, sleeve length, waistband position, and shoulder alignment with anatomically correct body proportions.
4. Face and hair: render the model with {모델 인종·헤어} and {모델 표정}, keeping the face cleanly lit, unobstructed, and consistent with commercial fashion photography.
5. Background and separation: use {배경} with soft edge separation and a subtle grounded shadow under the feet so the figure feels physically present, not floating.
6. Lighting treatment: apply {라이팅} with visible fabric texture, crisp contour separation, and controlled highlights that do not wash out the garment color.
7. Camera framing: shoot in the style of {카메라}, with a vertical lookbook composition, full-body clarity, and minimal perspective distortion for catalog use.
8. Fidelity check: maintain exact garment shape, color, texture, and fit from the reference, with no extra accessories, no changed branding, and no unexpected styling additions.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: none in the image unless source text exists; if any UI-like text is added, use Pretendard Medium or Noto Sans KR SemiBold, 22–34px, clean catalog layout.
- Color palette: {배경} values, plus neutral studio whites, soft beige, and garment-authentic source colors; avoid saturation shifts and preserve original material tone.
- Border/shadow: no frame border; use a soft realistic ground shadow, about 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 12–18% opacity, to anchor the model.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Phase One IQ4, 80mm f/4 lookbook standard, full-frame equivalent feel, minimal distortion, sharp garment detail.
- Lighting: 3-light studio setup with key light from upper-left at 45°, soft fill from front-right, and a subtle rim light from behind to separate the outline and emphasize texture.
- Color grade: clean editorial neutrals with accurate garment color reproduction, light warm-white balance, and controlled contrast similar to premium ecommerce lookbooks.

[6. MOOD]
Premium fashion e-commerce hero image — modern lookbook spread with a COS / Acne Studios catalog feel.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: none required unless source garment contains Korean text; if so, preserve it exactly as printed in the reference.
- Preserve the exact garment from the reference image: pattern, color, texture, fabric, stitching, label, branding, cut, and proportion must remain unchanged.
- When a person reference is provided, preserve their face features exactly.
- The model must wear the garment naturally with anatomically correct proportions and realistic fabric drape.
- No extra accessories, no altered silhouette, no cropped feet/hands, and no unexpected scene elements.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Garment redesign, pattern change, color shift, texture change, label manipulation, or logo distortion
- Face deformation, identity drift, age shift, or race alteration
- Sexualized pose, nudity, or exposure emphasis
- Exaggerated body proportions, warped fit, or impossible garment drape
- Cropped hands, feet, or head
- Any added prop, background object, or advertisement copy that was not requested

[1. PURPOSE]
4컷 i2i outfit try-on collage for personal styling, showing the same garment worn by the same person in four different real-life situations.
Social-media-shareable vertical editorial layout that feels like a polished Instagram fashion diary: realistic locations, readable Korean labels, natural lifestyle details, and clear variation across contexts while preserving the outfit exactly.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the same model across all 4 panels, with consistent face identity preserved from {원본 인물} and the same garment from {원본 옷} applied naturally in every scene.
- Use a structured 2x2 grid or a tall 1x4 strip depending on {레이아웃}, with equal panel sizing, thin dividers, consistent gutters, and a refined editorial card layout suitable for 1024x1536.
- Add a small top editorial header area: Korean title text such as “상황별 룩 4컷”, subtitle “같은 옷, 다른 순간”, date label “2026.05.01”, and small handle “@my_style.archive”.
- Each panel should feel like a distinct environment matching {시츄에이션 4종}, with believable props, architectural details, people or silhouettes in the distance, signage blur, tables, bags, devices, or travel objects appropriate to the scene.
- Backgrounds should shift by scenario: luxury hotel lobby for wedding guest, modern office for interview, warm cafe or restaurant for date, and overseas street or airport for travel.
- Add small Korean scene captions inside or beneath each panel: “결혼식 하객룩”, “면접룩”, “데이트룩”, “여행룩”, plus short secondary notes like “PM 2:30 호텔 로비”, “AM 10:00 인터뷰”, “PM 7:00 와인바”, “DAY 1 출국길”.
- Include tiny Instagram-card style UI details near the bottom: “♡ 12.4K   댓글 248   공유   저장”, plus hashtags such as “#상황별룩 #데일리룩 #착장기록”.
- Leave enough readable room for captions and full-body outfit visibility; do not crop the garment awkwardly at joints, sleeve ends, waistline, or hemline.
- Keep {포즈·표정} specific to each situation, while preserving the same person’s facial structure, natural body proportions, and realistic garment fit.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Panel 1 (wedding guest, hotel lobby): dress the model in {원본 옷} with polished posture, elegant standing pose, refined luxury-hotel interior with marble flooring, brass railings, chandelier reflections, floral arrangements, soft guest silhouettes, and a small location label reading “결혼식 하객룩”.
- Panel 2 (interview, office): keep the exact same garment on the same model, but place them in a modern office setting with glass partition, desk, laptop, notebook, pen, visitor chair, muted corporate wall art, and documentary-style professional framing; add label “면접룩”.
- Panel 3 (date, cafe or restaurant): show the same outfit in a relaxed social setting with warm tabletop props, coffee cup or wine glass, small dessert plate, menu card, candlelight, blurred bokeh lights, and a gentle conversational pose; add label “데이트룩”.
- Panel 4 (travel, overseas street or airport): use the same clothing and person reference in a kinetic travel scene with street perspective or airport terminal depth, rolling suitcase, passport pouch or tote, departure-board blur, crosswalk or gate signage, and walking motion; add label “여행룩”.
- Add subtle editorial stickers or tags that fit the theme, such as “OOTD”, “STYLE CHECK”, “4 SCENES”, and “SAME ITEM”, placed like small magazine annotations without covering the outfit.
- Apply scenario-specific color treatment from {컬러·톤} while maintaining the garment’s exact design fidelity across all four panels.
- Match camera treatment from {카메라} across the grid so the outfit reads consistently, with only scene, pose, lighting, and styling context changing between panels.
- Preserve all visible details of {원본 옷}: pattern, color, texture, fabric weave, stitching, label placement, branding, cut, silhouette, and proportion must remain faithful to the source image.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard SemiBold or Noto Sans KR Medium for Korean labels, 18–24px equivalent for scene titles and 10–14px equivalent for micro captions; use crisp editorial spacing with no decorative script.
- Text to render in Korean should include: “상황별 룩 4컷”, “같은 옷, 다른 순간”, “결혼식 하객룩”, “면접룩”, “데이트룩”, “여행룩”, “2026.05.01”, “#상황별룩 #데일리룩 #착장기록”.
- Color palette: wedding amber, office cool gray, date warm beige, travel cinematic blue; keep neutrals like #F4F1EA, #D9D9D9, #2B2B2B, with scenario accents from {컬러·톤}.
- Border/shadow: thin 1px divider lines in soft gray, subtle 8–12px blurred panel shadow at 10–15% opacity, refined editorial card edges, and small UI icons that feel printed or overlaid on a social post.
- The final image should feel content-rich and realistic, with each panel carrying its own story while maintaining a cohesive fashion lookbook grid.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Sony A7R V with 50mm f/2.8 for consistent full-body garment clarity, or Leica M11 with 35mm f/2 for a slightly more lifestyle editorial feel.
- Lighting: wedding panel with soft window light from upper-left and gentle fill from right; interview panel with even office daylight from front-left; date panel with warm practical ambient light and soft key from table-side; travel panel with late-afternoon daylight or overcast diffused light for a cinematic street look.
- Color grade: polished editorial realism with scenario-based grading — classic amber for wedding, clean neutral for interview, warm cafe beige for date, and cooler cinematic blue-gray for travel.
- Material realism: keep fabric texture, seam tension, wrinkles, drape, shadows, sleeve shape, hem behavior, and body contact consistent with the original garment and the model’s movement.
- Background realism: include natural depth of field, reflections on glass or marble, soft motion blur in distant pedestrians, readable-but-not-dominant signage, and everyday objects that make each scene believable.

[6. MOOD]
Fashion editorial lookbook meets personal Instagram styling archive — like a polished Vogue Korea or Harper’s Bazaar street-style spread adapted into a practical “same item, four situations” social post.
Warm, useful, aspirational, and realistic, with the feeling of an actual outfit record saved for styling reference.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: all labels, captions, hashtags, UI text, date labels, and scene notes must be rendered in flawless Korean without broken characters.
- Preserve the exact face features from {원본 인물}; do not alter age, race, expression identity, facial structure, hairstyle identity, or recognizable facial proportions.
- Replicate the exact garment from {원본 옷} in every panel — preserve precise pattern, color, texture, fabric, stitching, label, branding, cut, silhouette, and proportion.
- All 4 panels must show the same person and same outfit, with only background, pose, lighting, and styling context changing.
- Respect {시츄에이션 4종}, {레이아웃}, {포즈·표정}, {컬러·톤}, {카메라}, and {비율} exactly as the main creative direction.
- Render the final composition as one complete vertical 1024x1536 image, not four separate files.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean fashion magazine editorial i2i portrait, full-body lookbook-style cover frame. Preserve the exact outfit and the person reference while transforming the image into a realistic high-end fashion magazine cover with layered editorial typography, issue metadata, short Korean feature blurbs, barcode area, and believable print-cover finishing.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {원본 인물} occupies 55–65% of the frame, full-body hero centered with a slight 3/4 angle and elegant restrained motion.
- Outfit focus: {원본 옷} must read clearly from head to toe; sleeves, hem, shoes, silhouette, textile texture, labels, and brand details remain visible while cover typography is arranged around the figure and never obscures key garment features.
- Background treatment: {배경·세트} as a polished fashion magazine set with controlled depth separation; use a refined beige, charcoal, or blue studio environment, or a conceptual set such as sculptural flowers, architectural blocks, reflective floor panels, fabric backdrops, or geometric structures.
- Magazine cover framing: vertical fashion-page composition with the subject fully visible, no crop at ankles or head, plus integrated cover elements including masthead, issue number, date label, price, barcode block, short feature blurbs, small credit text, and model-name credit.
- Cover text layout: place a large fashion masthead near the top such as “OURS MAGAZINE” or “LOOK ISSUE”; add realistic Korean cover lines around the subject, for example “나다운 선택이 가장 좋은 답”, “이번 시즌 실루엣”, “하루를 바꾸는 옷”, and “STYLE NOTE”.
- Customizable placeholders: {매거진 톤}, {포즈·각도}, {라이팅}, {컬러 팔레트}, {카메라·렌즈}, {비율}

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Hero figure: place {원본 인물} as the primary editorial subject, standing naturally with confident posture, keeping the face proportions faithful to the reference and the outfit silhouette intact.
2) Garment fidelity: reproduce {원본 옷} exactly as seen in the reference image — preserve pattern, color, texture, fabric drape, stitching, label, branding, cut, and overall proportion with no redesign.
3) Set and separation: build {배경·세트} with a premium studio atmosphere; include realistic floor contact, soft shadow, visible material surfaces, and subtle environmental depth that supports the fashion story.
4) Pose and energy: apply {포즈·각도} as a fashion editorial pose with slight torso turn, relaxed arms, and a composed runway-to-magazine feel.
5) Lighting pass: apply {라이팅} so the clothing structure, seams, folds, accessories, and body contour are clearly modeled without harsh clipping or flat lighting.
6) Color system: harmonize the full image with {컬러 팔레트}; keep skin tones natural while ensuring the outfit remains the visual anchor.
7) Capture language: render as a premium magazine photo using {카메라·렌즈} with crisp textile detail, realistic depth of field, and print-ready clarity.
8) Magazine publishing layer: add believable editorial cover components — “VOL.1052”, “2026년 5월호”, “₩8,500”, a small barcode area at lower corner, tiny spine-like vertical text, photographer/styling credits, and model-name credit such as “MODEL {원본 인물}”.
9) Format finish: maintain {비율} as a tall editorial page layout, with clean print alignment, realistic cover hierarchy, and cover lines composed around the full-body silhouette.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use fashion-magazine cover typography with a large refined masthead, bold Korean main cover line, and 2–3 short feature blurbs. Use Pretendard, Helvetica Neue, Didot-like serif, or clean Korean editorial type; mix large 90–150px masthead scale with medium 28–48px blurbs and tiny 10–18px credits.
- Required Korean text elements in image: include short, legible cover text such as “나다운 선택이 가장 좋은 답”, “이번 시즌 실루엣”, “하루를 바꾸는 옷”, “STYLE NOTE”, “2026년 5월호”, and “VOL.1052”.
- Editorial microcopy: add small realistic text blocks such as “FASHION / BEAUTY / CULTURE”, “PHOTOGRAPHY BY OURS STUDIO”, “STYLING NOTE”, “서울 에디션”, and a lower-corner barcode label.
- Color palette: use the exact mood of {컬러 팔레트}, with refined editorial tones such as matte beige #E8DDCF, charcoal #2B2B2B, deep navy #22324A, muted cream #F5F1EA, warm gray #B9AFA3, or soft black #111111 depending on the selected tone.
- Print finish: emulate a premium glossy or satin magazine cover with realistic ink density, gentle paper sheen, accurate type layering, subtle soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 14% opacity, and crisp high-resolution edges.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: {카메라·렌즈} rendered like a high-end fashion editorial shot, e.g. Hasselblad H6D with 80mm f/4 or Phase One IQ4 with 110mm f/2.8, shallow but controlled depth of field.
- Lighting: studio key light at 45° from front-left or front-right, with soft rim light to shape the silhouette and a gentle fill to preserve fabric detail; keep specular highlights controlled and premium.
- Color grade: magazine editorial grading with clean neutral whites, nuanced skin tones, and a tone-matched palette that can lean VOGUE classic, ELLE polished, NYLON youthful, W dark, or GQ charcoal depending on {매거진 톤}.
- Surface realism: show believable studio floor texture, gentle shadow falloff, fabric micro-texture, natural hair detail, true-to-reference facial features, and realistic interaction between the cover typography and photographed subject.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean fashion editorial cover — a Condé Nast / Vogue-style cover shoot with the polish of a luxury lookbook, the immediacy of a real monthly magazine issue, and a refined runway-backed fashion spread feel. The final image should feel published, collectible, and content-rich rather than like a blank studio mockup.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: all rendered Korean cover text must be legible and natural, especially “나다운 선택이 가장 좋은 답”, “이번 시즌 실루엣”, “하루를 바꾸는 옷”, “2026년 5월호”, “서울 에디션”, and “VOL.1052”.
- Preserve identity and garment exactly: the face must match {원본 인물} faithfully, and the clothing must match {원본 옷} without any change to pattern, color, fabric, stitching, label, branding, or fit.
- Composition invariants: full-body editorial framing, natural garment drape, realistic anatomy, correct hands and feet, no distortion of body proportions, and cover typography must not hide essential outfit details.
- Magazine realism: include masthead, issue/date/price label, 2–3 Korean feature blurbs, barcode area, small spine or credit text, and model-name credit while maintaining a premium fashion-cover hierarchy.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized celebrity likeness

[1. PURPOSE]
Lifestyle i2i portrait combining the exact outfit from the clothing reference with the preserved face from the person reference.
Create a real-looking Korean daily-life editorial image for lookbook, SNS profile, OOTD archive, and personal brand use, with believable location details and a candid moment atmosphere.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {원본 인물} occupies 55–65% of the frame, framed as a natural half-body or 3/4 body lifestyle shot.
- Outfit focus: {원본 옷} is the visual anchor, shown clearly enough for fabric, fit, silhouette, seams, label, and natural drape recognition.
- Scene setting: {시츄에이션} with realistic environmental depth: add natural lifestyle context such as a café table edge, street curb, plants, books, phone, tote bag, cup, wall texture, window reflection, signage, or passersby blur only when it fits the situation.
- Pose direction: {포즈·자세} with relaxed weight shift, believable hand placement, casual body tension, and a spontaneous candid rhythm.
- Background treatment: location-specific and lived-in, with layered midground/background elements, realistic textures, and mild depth-of-field separation that keeps the face and garment readable.
- Framing: vertical portrait composition with editorial breathing room, but include enough surrounding environment to make the scene feel like an authentic day-in-the-life photograph.
- Lifestyle detail: include 1–3 subtle personal objects that support the moment, such as a phone in hand, folded receipt, reusable cup, small accessory, shopping bag, magazine, notebook, or transit card, without covering the outfit.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Foreground subject block: {원본 인물} rendered with face identity preserved exactly, natural expression, realistic skin texture, fine hair detail, and believable eye catchlight.
- Garment block: {원본 옷} matched precisely in pattern, color, texture, stitching, label placement, branding, cut, fit, and proportion; no redesign, no reinterpretation.
- Scene integration block: place the subject inside {시츄에이션} so the environment feels like a real candid moment rather than a studio cutout; match foot placement, shadows, reflections, and scale to the location.
- Pose execution block: {포즈·자세} should look spontaneous and unposed, with anatomy, shoulders, arms, fingers, torso angle, and garment folds aligned naturally.
- Light shaping block: {조명} should define the face and outfit with soft shadow falloff, subtle highlights on fabric texture, and gentle separation from the background.
- Color finishing block: {컬러 그레이딩} should unify skin tones, fabric tones, props, and background tones without oversaturation.
- Camera framing block: {카메라·렌즈} should imply a polished lifestyle editorial look with realistic perspective, clean subject compression, and natural background falloff.
- Format block: {비율} as a vertical portrait composition with balanced top-to-bottom visual weight and enough context to read the situation clearly.
- Editorial overlay block: add a small diary-style OOTD caption area in the lower corner or along one side, designed like a subtle SNS archive sticker, not a commercial advertisement.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: allow small on-image editorial micro-text using Pretendard Medium or Noto Sans KR Medium; use clean Korean captions, date/location labels, and tiny tag-style stickers that feel like a personal OOTD diary.
- Suggested rendered text elements: small label “오늘의 착장”, date stamp “2026.05.01”, caption “가볍게 걷는 오후”, tiny tag “#데일리룩”. Keep text crisp and correctly spelled in Korean.
- Color palette: preserve the exact garment colors from {원본 옷}, then support with muted urban neutrals such as warm gray, cream, soft taupe, charcoal, desaturated background tones, and small realistic accent colors from props or signage.
- Detail richness: include real-world texture such as concrete grain, wood table surface, glass reflections, fabric weave, paper edges, metal fixtures, soft street shadows, or window highlights as appropriate to {시츄에이션}.
- Border/shadow: use soft natural shadow under chin and around body edges, 8px y-offset, 18px blur, 14% opacity, with realistic contact shadows on nearby surfaces.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Sony A7R V with 85mm f/2 look for a portrait lookbook feel, or Leica Q3 28mm f/2.8 look if the scene needs more environment; realistic depth and clean subject separation.
- Lighting: natural window light from the side or golden hour side light, with soft shadow roll-off and a subtle fill from the opposite side to keep face and garment readable.
- Color grade: restrained 90s film editorial grading with slight warm highlights, muted midtones, and gently lifted blacks; cinematic but realistic.
- Texture: retain fine photographic grain, natural lens rendering, gentle highlight bloom, realistic skin pores, fabric weave, and environmental imperfections.

[6. MOOD]
Polished Korean lifestyle editorial — like a modern lookbook spread from Kinfolk meets a restrained 90s fashion diary, with an authentic OOTD snapshot feeling and enough everyday detail to feel personally lived-in.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: if text appears in the rendered image, spell these exactly: “오늘의 착장”, “2026.05.01”, “가볍게 걷는 오후”, “#데일리룩”.
- Identity preservation: preserve the face features of {원본 인물} exactly.
- Garment preservation: reproduce the exact garment from {원본 옷} — preserve precise pattern, color, texture, fabric, stitching, label, branding, cut, and proportion.
- Natural wear: the model wears the garment naturally, with realistic drape, folds, tension points, and interaction with the pose.
- No redesign: do not alter the outfit into a different style, and do not change the person’s facial identity.
- Prop placement: any added lifestyle object must support {시츄에이션} and must not obscure important garment details, face, hands, labels, or silhouette.
- Realistic integration: shadows, reflections, scale, depth of field, and background perspective must match the subject and camera angle.

- Fake official seals / certifications

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Upper header zone: place {한 줄} as a crisp Korean title, horizontally aligned and legible against the bright travel background.
2. Travel metadata strip: directly under or beside the title, add {위치라벨} · {날짜} · {시간} · {날씨} in small editorial text with a pin icon and thin divider line.
3. Main hero zone: show {참고 이미지} as the clear focal point, cropped from chest-up or waist-up depending on source image, with natural expression and travel-ready posture.
4. Styling cue layer: add {소품} in a way that looks like it belongs in a real arrival snapshot, including natural fabric folds, camera strap tension, hat shadow, and hand contact.
5. Destination atmosphere layer: build {여행지} through Parisian-style street cues such as cream stone façades, wrought-iron balcony hints, café awnings, flower stand colors, taxi blur, sidewalk reflections, and a distant landmark-like silhouette if appropriate.
6. Social caption layer: place {계정}, {서브캡션}, and {해시태그} near the lower area like an Instagram card, with tiny save/share/bookmark icons and a page-dot detail.
7. Color integration: apply {컬러} across background grading, accessory highlights, typography accents, sticker shapes, and warm reflections so the whole frame feels like one coherent travel memory.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR, SemiBold for the title, 34–44px equivalent on 1024px canvas; supporting text in Regular 18–22px equivalent; metadata in 13–16px equivalent.
- Color palette: pastel spring pink, cream, soft sky blue, muted lavender, and gold accent; include gentle warm highlights like #F7E7C6, #F4D9D1, #EAEFF7, #D9D0F2, #C8A96B.
- Graphic treatment: use postcard-style paper grain, translucent rounded labels, thin gold divider lines, tiny pin/save/share icons, and one or two playful sticker shapes without overpowering the face.
- Text hierarchy: title first, location/date second, caption/hashtags third; all Korean text must remain sharp, correctly spaced, and readable at 1024x1024.
- Realism details: include believable street textures, soft background pedestrians, café table edges, reflection highlights, and natural travel clutter such as a bag strap, ticket corner, or camera lens cap.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 50mm full-frame portrait look, f/2.2, natural selfie perspective, moderate depth of field, realistic handheld framing.
- Lighting: bright overcast daylight or soft morning window light from upper-left, with a faint warm fill from the right to echo the gold palette.
- Color grade: pastel spring travel editorial with gentle warm highlights, clean whites, and slightly softened contrast; keep skin tones natural.
- Rendering quality: realistic facial likeness from the reference image, natural skin texture, believable hair detail, accurate fabric texture, and subtle lens bokeh in the background.

[6. MOOD]
A personal travel-journal editorial — like a polished Instagram arrival story with a Condé Nast Traveler snapshot feel, warm, excited, slightly dreamy, and authentically just-arrived.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear exactly and correctly when using defaults: "드디어, 처음 본 파리", "PARIS · 에펠탑 근처", "2026.05.01", "@my.travel.note".

- The image must feel like a real personal arrival moment, with candid posture, natural hands, realistic selfie proportions, and believable travel accessories.
- Keep the destination recognizable through real street atmosphere, layered signage fragments, café textures, and soft urban depth rather than a flat tourist advertisement.

- Background surfaces should feel like a realistic beauty desk or warm ivory studio wall, with subtle paper texture, soft beige gradient, and small lifestyle details such as tiny shade swatches or cosmetic color chips integrated into the graphic frame.
- Add stage labels, date/location label, account handle, short caption, hashtag-style text, and small save/share micro icons so the card feels like a finished social-media beauty post rather than a plain comparison grid.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header band: At the top, place {카드 제목} in bold Korean typography, with {계정명} near the upper-left and a small date/location line reading {촬영일} · {위치} near the upper-right.
- Panel 1 (left 33%): {참고 이미지} in a natural bare-face look, evenly lit, with realistic skin texture, visible natural complexion, neutral expression, and the caption from {단계 3종} reading “민낯”.
- Panel 2 (center 34%): {참고 이미지} with light daily makeup, subtle base, defined brows, soft blush, gentle lip tint, and the same pose and framing, captioned “데일리”.
- Panel 3 (right 33%): {참고 이미지} with full makeup, stronger eye definition, contour, highlight, richer lip color, and preserved identity/camera angle, captioned “풀 메이크업”.
- Label strip: Add compact Korean labels beneath each panel, plus a small beauty-note line such as {피부 타입 메모} and {제품 메모} in a lower information strip.
- Footer social bar: Include {짧은 캡션}, {해시태그}, and tiny Instagram-style micro icons such as “♡ 2.4만   💬 128   ↗ 공유   🔖 저장” aligned along the bottom edge.
- Global consistency: Keep {조명} and {컬러 톤} visually matched across all three panels so the comparison feels controlled, believable, and editorial.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR, semibold for panel labels, 24–32px on a 1024x1024 canvas, crisp legibility, slightly increased tracking, with smaller 14–18px metadata text for handle, date, location, notes, and icons.
- Color palette: soft nude beige, ivory, pale peach, warm taupe, muted rose, light gray; reference tones from {컬러 톤}, using gentle accent chips for cosmetic shade swatches.
- Graphic details: thin white or light gray dividers, soft rounded label pills, subtle paper-grain overlay, delicate dotted guide marks, small blush/lip color swatches, and a refined editorial footer bar.
- Border/shadow: thin ivory frame lines and very light gray rules, subtle card shadow around 4px y-offset, 10px blur, 10–15% opacity.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 50mm portrait look at f/4, front-facing beauty photography framing, tightly cropped around the face and upper shoulders.
- Lighting: even natural window light from front-left at about 45°, soft fill on the opposite side, gentle natural shadows, and matched exposure across all three stages.
- Color grade: restrained nude-beige grading with slightly warm skin tones, low contrast, and gentle highlight roll-off.
- Retouching style: realistic beauty retouching that keeps pores, natural skin texture, lip texture, and small facial details while making the infographic feel polished.

[6. MOOD]
Clean beauty editorial infographic — similar to a Korean skincare brand comparison post combined with an Instagram beauty diary card, warm, personal, polished, and realistic.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문구: “민낯”, “데일리”, “풀 메이크업”, “{카드 제목}”, “{계정명}”, “{촬영일}”, “{위치}”.
- Render the caption and metadata clearly in Korean: “{짧은 캡션}”, “{피부 타입 메모}”, “{제품 메모}”, “{해시태그}”.
- Same-person consistency: all three panels must depict the exact same person from {참고 이미지}, with no facial identity drift.
- Maintain the same crop, angle, and framing logic across all three panels for a true comparison.
- Keep the makeup progression realistic and visually separated by stage: natural bare face → daily makeup → full makeup, with believable cosmetics and skin finish.
- The finished image should look like a complete 1024x1024 Korean beauty comparison post with header, labels, notes, social micro icons, and refined decorative graphics.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or implying a real public figure identity

Show {스타일 4종} on the same face with readable hairstyle differences, as if the image is a saved Korean beauty salon proof card for choosing a new look.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the face and shoulders in a balanced 2x2 grid, with each quadrant taking equal visual weight and consistent head size across all four panels.
- Keep {참고 이미지} as the identity anchor; preserve the same facial proportions, expression range, skin tone, and camera angle in every panel.
- Use {레이아웃} with thin dividing lines, even gutters, and a polished editorial card frame; keep hair silhouettes separated clearly between panels.
- Dress the subject in {의상}, cropped consistently at upper chest level, with realistic fabric folds, neckline detail, and subtle styling consistency.
- Set a smooth {배경} backdrop with gentle salon-studio atmosphere: faint wall texture, soft gradient depth, and subtle reflected light that makes hair volume readable.
- Use {비율} with a square social-card composition including a small top title strip and a compact footer information bar.
- Add realistic Korean card details: title text “헤어스타일 4종 비교”, date label “2026.05.01”, location label “서울 성수동”, handle “@hair.note”, small save/share micro icons, and a tiny decorative comb or scissors sticker near the footer.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Panel 1 (top-left): Show the first hairstyle from {스타일 4종} as a neat, natural cut with detailed hairline, realistic root direction, and salon-finished volume. Add a small label: “STYLE 01”.
- Panel 2 (top-right): Show the second hairstyle from {스타일 4종} with a clearly different length and silhouette, while preserving identical face placement and shoulder framing. Add a small label: “STYLE 02”.
- Panel 3 (bottom-left): Show the third hairstyle from {스타일 4종} with visible texture change, such as wave pattern or layered movement, rendered as a believable salon-style result. Add a small label: “STYLE 03”.
- Panel 4 (bottom-right): Show the fourth hairstyle from {스타일 4종} with the strongest shape contrast, such as tied-up height, ponytail lift, short crop, or bold layered outline depending on {스타일 4종}, while keeping facial identity unchanged. Add a small label: “STYLE 04”.
- Under or beside each style label, include short Korean comparison notes such as “얼굴형 보완”, “볼륨감”, “손질 쉬움”, “분위기 전환”, matched naturally to the hairstyle.
- Apply consistent cutout edges, soft shadowing, and matching studio perspective so each panel feels like one unified hairstyle proof sheet from the same session.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR, medium to semibold weight, 24–34px for panel labels and 14–18px for micro text; use crisp charcoal text with slightly tight Korean letter spacing.
- Color palette: neutral gray #B8B8B8, soft white #F7F7F5, charcoal #2B2B2B, light silver #D9D9D9, with a muted beige accent #D7C8B8 for tags or stickers.
- Border/shadow: thin 1px dividers in light gray, subtle 4px drop shadow with 12px blur at 12% opacity for each portrait cutout, plus a soft rounded card container.
- Graphic details: add small pill-shaped tags, tiny checklist marks, a page indicator “1/1”, and a footer note “상담용 시뮬레이션” in Korean, all integrated like a premium Korean beauty app card.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]

- Lighting: softbox key light from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from front-right, very soft shadow falloff to keep hair texture, highlights, and strand separation legible in all four panels.
- Color grade: cool-neutral editorial grade with slightly desaturated grays, natural skin tones, soft salon highlights, and realistic hair shine.
- Rendering: photorealistic beauty retouching with visible individual strands, natural flyaways, realistic scalp/root transitions, and believable fabric and skin texture.

[6. MOOD]
Modern Korean beauty editorial meets practical salon consultation card — polished, friendly, realistic, and ready to save or share on Instagram.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: {참고 이미지}, {스타일 4종}, {레이아웃}, {의상}, {배경}, {비율}
- Same person identity must remain consistent across all 4 panels: identical face, age appearance, skin tone, and camera angle.
- Hair must look physically plausible in every panel, with natural roots, believable strand flow, correct hairline continuity, and salon-realistic volume.
- Render Korean in-image text clearly: “헤어스타일 4종 비교”, “STYLE 01”, “STYLE 02”, “STYLE 03”, “STYLE 04”, “2026.05.01”, “서울 성수동”, “@hair.note”, “상담용 시뮬레이션”.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Broken Korean characters

[INPUT]
- reference_image: {참고 이미지}
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
A square self-unboxing product shot for social media, centered on the creator opening a newly received item with an authentic first-impression feel.
Korean lifestyle creator post style, bright tabletop composition, identity-preserving framing, designed as a finished Instagram feed card in {비율}.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {참고 이미지} is placed as the primary human subject, occupying about 55% of the frame, with the product box and unpacking action clearly readable at chest-to-table level.
- Composition: camera angle slightly above eye level, angled down 15–20° to show both face and desktop; keep the face and {제품} equally legible.
- Background treatment: realistic Korean home-studio interior with a clean white wall, light wood desk surface, soft paper texture, a small desk lamp, tape roll, receipt slip, courier label, and everyday unboxing traces.
- Layout: face in the upper center, hands and box opening zone in the lower center, with a subtle social-post overlay layer placed along the top-left and bottom-right without covering the eyes, hands, or product silhouette.
- Styling anchors: emphasize {표정}, {소품}, {컬러}, a visible product label reading “{제품라벨}”, and realistic packaging layers that make the first-opening moment feel candid.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Upper area (top 25%): show the subject’s face visible and softly lit, reacting naturally; add a small profile-style header label with “@{계정명}” and “{날짜위치}”.
2. Center area (middle 40%): {참고 이미지} shown naturally reacting to the unboxing, with eyes focused on {제품} and a clear expression matching {표정}; include torn tape ends, folded instruction leaflet corners, and a partially visible thank-you card.
3. Lower center area (bottom 35%): {제품} partially removed from the box, with {소품} arranged in a realistic unpacking sequence — outer box, inner molded tray, protective sleeve, cable pouch, and protective film layered in order.
4. Surface detail: show light wood desk grain, box flaps, air-cap packaging, small scissors, shipping sticker, and folded receipt angled toward the camera for easy readability.
5. Social card details: add Instagram-style micro icons for like/comment/share/save, a small reaction tag “{반응태그}”, the caption “{짧은캡션}”, and hashtag-style text “{해시태그}” integrated as tasteful overlay graphics.
6. Color harmony: apply {컬러} as the dominant palette across the desk, packaging, background accents, and UI overlay; keep warm whites, light oak tones, pale gray, and soft beige balanced.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Medium and Pretendard SemiBold; profile header 22–26px, caption 24–30px, hashtag text 18–22px, micro UI labels 14–18px.
- Color palette: {컬러} should read as soft white, pale beige, and light oak tones; use accent gray #D9D9D9, warm off-white #F7F6F2, graphite text #2B2B2B, and soft blue-gray accent #AEB8C2.
- Overlay design: add translucent rounded rectangles, small sticker-style tags, tiny save/share icons, and a subtle date/location pill that feels like a real Korean creator upload.
- Border/shadow: subtle soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity under the box, product pieces, and UI stickers; use soft rounded UI edges and natural contact shadows.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame 50mm lens at f/2.8, natural perspective, crisp focus on face and product with mild background separation.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from front-right, controlled highlights on plastic film, realistic reflections on the product surface.
- Color grade: clean editorial neutral grade with slightly warm highlights, balanced whites, and mild desaturation for a premium everyday product-photo look.

[6. MOOD]
Modern Korean lifestyle editorial — like a polished creator diary post, premium desk setup update, and sincere first-impression unboxing moment captured in a bright Seoul home studio.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render all visible Korean cleanly and fully legibly, especially “@{계정명}”, “{날짜위치}”, “{짧은캡션}”, “{해시태그}”, and “{반응태그}”.
- Identity: the person in {참고 이미지} must remain clearly identifiable as the same person, with natural facial proportions and realistic hand anatomy.
- Hands: anatomically correct, exactly 5 fingers per hand, properly holding, lifting, peeling, or opening the packaging.
- Product realism: {제품} should look newly opened, with believable box fit, protective film, cable pouch, paper inserts, courier sticker, and desk-scale proportions.
- Social post realism: the Instagram-style UI elements must look like a creator-designed overlay, not an official app screenshot; keep them secondary to the face and unboxing action.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized celebrity likeness
